subject: Request: Custom availability exhibit + onboarding runbook
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@healtech.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healtech.io>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: HealTech availability exhibit ask

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement asked us to get a tailored availability exhibit attached to our MSA that explicitly covers regional failover and a two-tiered latency credit schedule for production traffic. Key asks below: 

- 99.95% monthly uptime across N. Virginia with documented failover to West Coast within 90s for control-plane routing events
- Latency credit bands tied to p95 and p99 for gen text requests (we proposed p95 < 500ms, p99 < 900ms)
- Evidence items: weekly uptime dashboard access, 90-day incident runbooks for any availability event > 1 hr
- Onboarding playbook describing cutover plan and telemetry integration for our infra team

We uploaded our requirements doc to the folder linked here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/healtech-reqs (attached healtech_requirements_v1.pdf). Can you propose language we can hand to legal? Also any impact on order form pricing/committed capacity would be helpful.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Lee
Head of Cloud Ops, HealTech Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@healtech.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 12:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealTech availability exhibit ask

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are two artifacts for initial review: a first-pass Availability Exhibit (redwood_availability_exhibit_draft.docx) and an Onboarding Runbook draft (onboarding_runbook_draft.pdf). High-level notes up front: 

- Coverage/Failover: we can commit to a 99.95% monthly uptime for the primary region with an operational failover SLA that targets control-plane route propagation within 90s for region-to-region failovers. We need to mark multi-region routing as a dependent capability (customer must enable regional replication in order form).
- Latency credits: we included a two-band credit schedule tied to p95/p99 for standard generation calls. The exhibit ties credits to per-API-token costs and caps cumulative monthly credits at 25% of monthly committed spend for the covered deployment.
- Evidence & telemetry: we can provide a read-only dashboard (weekly) plus a 90-day post-incident packet. For audit-grade evidence (SOC-level logs) we'll need a separate request and may involve enterprise logging retention add-on.
- Onboarding: the runbook includes a 6-week cutover plan, prep checklist for your infra team, and telemetry endpoints plus sample Grafana dashboards.

Potential impacts to order form/pricing: to guarantee the 90s failover routing and the tighter latency bands we recommend reserved capacity (Dedicated) with burst protection. I asked Ben to run a quick delta on monthly unit economics for a 2x reserved profile vs standard hosted.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You and procurement review the attached language and mark any hard no's vs negotiable items.
2) If acceptable, Naomi can spin a redline-ready doc and route via DocuSign to get exhibit attached to the MSA + order form.
3) We will coordinate a joint ops sync (30–45 min) to walk the runbook and telemetry integration.

I'll be offline after 5pm PT but Ben and Naomi are on point for the pricing/contract threads.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_availability_exhibit_draft.docx, onboarding_runbook_draft.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealTech availability exhibit ask — cost & runbook notes

Karthik/Naomi —

Quick take from pricing/solutions after reviewing the draft exhibit and the onboarding runbook: 

- Cost: Locking 90s regional failover + tightened p99 band increases expected unit cost ~18–22% vs the baseline hosted catalog for the same token throughput. I captured line-item deltas in cost-impact-redlines.xlsx.
- Dedicated ask: recommend a minimum Dedicated pool sized to cover sustained peak concurrency; otherwise credits/penalties exposure goes up. We should tie the order form to a minimum committed TPU or GPU hour figure to make the exhibit operationally feasible.
- Evidence: solutions requests we include scheduled weekly SLA exports (read-only) and a single 90-day incident packet per qualifying event. Anything more frequent or raw-logs will need an add-on.

Action items for Naomi: please prepare a redline packet with the exhibit + normative order form clauses that call out: 1) required Dedicated sizing, 2) failover activation steps and customer responsibilities, 3) credit cap and calculation method. I attached my spreadsheet with suggested numbers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: cost-impact-redlines.xlsx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@healtech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Consolidated exhibit redlines and next steps (DocuSign ready)

Hannah —

Thanks for your patience. We've consolidated feedback and attached the redline packet referenced in earlier notes. Summary of what's changed vs your ask: 

- We accepted the 99.95% primary-region uptime with a defined Regional Failover Procedure (RFP). The RFP is now explicit about failover initiation triggers, expected automation window (targeted 90s), and required customer responses (DNS TTL, regional replication flag).
- Latency bands: we tightened p95/p99 thresholds but added a credit cap (25% monthly committed spend) and a per-incident credit floor to avoid micro-credits for short blips.
- Evidence: weekly read-only dashboard exports and a 90-day incident packet for qualifying events are included. Audit-grade logs and SOC evidence remain a paid add-on per the exhibit.
- Order form language: added a Dedicated capacity minimum in section 2 of the order form (minimum committed GPU hours) and a billing reconciliation clause if committed capacity is not met.

Next steps and timelines: 
1) Please review the attached redline packet and call out any absolute blockers by EOD Tue, 06 Jul 2027.
2) If no hard blockers, we'll convert to a clean exhibit and route via DocuSign (link below) for signature and MSA attachment.
3) Schedule the onboarding ops sync (we're proposing Wed 14 Jul, 30 minutes).

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/AAA-EXHIBIT-HLT-2027
Draft files: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Aexample-availability-exhibit

Best,
